claim: For five voters with strict single-peaked rankings on the ordered alternatives \(0,1,\ldots,m-1\), each approving exactly their top \(k\) alternatives, a unique top-\(k\)-approval winner exists for some profile if and only if \(m\ge 2k-1\). Over all such profiles with a unique winner \(w\), the maximum distance from the median peak \(h\) is \[D_5(m,k)=\max |w-h|=\begin{cases}k-1,&2k-1\le m<5k-1,\m-3k,&m\ge5k-1.\end{cases}\]

correctness.rationale: The proof gives a complete upper bound in the near and far regimes, proves the exact feasibility condition \(m\ge2k-1\), and supplies explicit single-peaked interval profiles attaining both branches. The far-regime inequalities imply m>=5k-1 and \(|w-h|\le m-3k\); all endpoints and the k=1 case are included.

value.rationale: This is a sharp, natural finite classification of the maximum spatial displacement of a unique fixed-k approval winner from the median voter. The exact transition \(\(\(m=5k-1\)\)\) separates a local bound k-1 from a linearly growing branch \(\(\(m-3k\)\)\), clarifying a limitation of the median-voter intuition for a widely studied scoring rule. The five-voter case is the smallest odd electorate with two voters on each side available to create the far-displacement regime.
